function: Joint device selection and aggregate (receive) beamforming for AirComp model aggregation in over-the-air federated learning (p. 1, 3).
system: K single-antenna devices, aggregator with N antennas (N=8 in CDF check, N=4 in FL runs, swept in Fig. 7); no RIS; frequency band not stated (p. 3, 6, 10).
method: Federated learning (ResNet18, local SGD) over AirComp; the aggregate beamformer is a random-sampling plus sorting scheme, not trained (p. 3, 5, 10).
data_channel: Synthetic i.i.d. Rayleigh channels hk~CN(0,I) (p. 3); non-i.i.d. CIFAR10 split for the FL task (p. 10); no standardized channel model or measurements.
test_conditions: No training/test channel split; Monte Carlo (1000 runs) sweeps of K, S, N and MSE threshold; CIFAR10 test accuracy for FL (p. 6, 9, 10).
baselines: Non-learned: Random+DC, Iterative (DC), l1+SDR [36]; earlier OTA-FL design: DC method of [31]; no neural-network beamforming baseline (p. 8-9).
metrics: Aggregate MSE/sigma^2, number of selected devices, and CIFAR10 test accuracy of the FL model (p. 9-10).
complexity: O(N+K log K) for MSE minimization, O(N+K) for device-count maximization; O(Nm(N+K log K)) with Nm sampled beamformers (p. 3, 5, 8).
q1_support: p. 3: "hk ∼ CN (0, I)" - custom i.i.d. Rayleigh simulator; no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel is used anywhere in the paper.
q2_support: p. 10: "classification tasks on the well-known CIFAR10 data sets" - the beamformer is untrained and the FL model is tested only on CIFAR10; no scenario, band or dataset unseen in training is reported.
q3_support: p. 9: "Novel DC Method [31]" - earlier published OTA-FL aggregation design compared on number of selected devices (p. 10, Fig. 8) and accuracy; p. 8: "Random+DC" is a non-learned baseline compared on MSE.
q4_support: p. 3: "low, which are O(N + K log K) and O(N + K)" - complexity of the proposed scheme, derived in Sec. III-B (p. 5).
q5_support: p. 10: "classification tasks on the well-known CIFAR10 data sets" - public dataset of the learning task only; channels are simulated and no code or data link or DOI is given.
notes: Included under the over-the-air FL rule: the learned element is the FL model (ResNet18 on CIFAR10, p. 10), while the proposed beamformer is a non-learned random-sampling scheme (p. 5). Area 7 because the problem is the aggregation itself (aggregate beamforming and device selection, p. 1). q3 rests on [31] as the earlier published aggregation design; Random+DC and Iterative are the paper's own heuristics and do not count as the learned baseline (p. 8). The aggregator has N>1 antennas, so the system check passes.
